title: Non-destructive measurement is not automatically non-perturbative
problem: A same-follicle observer can preserve unit identity while still changing the later follicle trajectory through illumination, fluorophore chemistry, heat, handling, environmental drift or repeated acquisition.

pass_rule.statistical: the full confidence interval for the observer effect on a declared downstream functional endpoint must lie inside a predeclared symmetric equivalence margin
design_obligations: at least one acquisition-dose or frequency challenge

unknown_rule: If the confidence interval overlaps an equivalence boundary, or any required design control is absent, measurement back-action remains UNKNOWN.
fail_rule: If the confidence interval lies wholly outside the equivalence region, the observer fails the back-action gate for that endpoint and acquisition regime.
important_non_equivalences: one safe acquisition regime != all acquisition regimes
photobleaching absence != absence of physiological phototoxicity
source_context: Li et al., Nature Communications 2026 used real-time confocal imaging to quantify intact human-HF width/contraction trajectories, making same-unit mechanical observation plausible.
Live-cell microscopy literature documents illumination- and fluorophore-associated phototoxicity and recommends explicit exposure and physiology controls.
HF01_implication: A live mechanical observer is not promoted to a same-follicle predictive probe until its later-growth/cycle back-action is bounded under the exact acquisition protocol used.
claim_boundary: This contract does not assert that the Li et al. imaging protocol caused material back-action; it defines the evidence required before HF01 reuses live imaging as a longitudinal state observer.
